one_liner: Senior DOJ acquisition policy expert who writes and interprets FAR-based procurement policy and advises the Office of Acquisition Management director.
fit_summary: This GS-14 contracting job requires at least 4 years of contracting experience, including one year at the GS-13 equivalent overseeing procurement programs and writing FAR-implementing policy, plus 24 semester hours in business-related fields. Daniel's policy knowledge and emergency-management consulting background don't show that hands-on acquisition work. Unless your IEM role was actually in federal contract management or acquisition policy, you likely won't pass the basic qualification screen.
eligibility: Open to the public (direct hire), so you do not need federal status, a clearance, or veterans' preference.

Basic qualification A: at least 4 years of contracting or related experience, with 1 year equivalent to GS-13 overseeing procurement activities AND advising on or developing FAR-implementing acquisition policy.

Basic qualification B: a 4-year bachelor's degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management. Transcripts are required.
You must pass the USA Hire online assessment at or above the cut score.
FAC-C Level III is preferred, though it is not required at appointment.
keywords: Office of Management and Budget initiatives
strategy: Before applying, check honestly whether your IEM work involved federal contracts (proposals, contract administration, FAR compliance, task-order management) for at least 4 years. If it didn't, skip this posting.

If it did, describe in your own words any work interpreting FAR clauses, managing contract deliverables, or advising clients on procurement rules. Don't copy the specialized-experience statement; HR will rule you ineligible if you repeat it verbatim.
Pull your transcripts now and count your business, economics, law, or management credits to confirm you have 24 semester hours.
Apply within 14 days of the July 27, 2026 opening to make the initial cut-off. Later applications are considered only if more vacancies come up.
Keep the resume to two pages, and list hours per week and month/year dates for each job.

Better near-term targets are GS-1102 entry roles (GS-7/9), FEMA or Virginia VDEM positions, emergency management jobs in Prince William County, or legislative staff roles that use your policy and relationship skills.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] on [contract/task order type] valued at [$X], ensuring deliverables complied with [FAR part/clause] over [timeframe].
Advised [client/team] on [procurement or grant policy topic], preparing [memos/briefings] that presented alternative courses of action to [senior officials].
Coordinated with [number] stakeholders across [agencies/jurisdictions] to [disaster recovery outcome], tracking [cost/compliance metric].
interview_questions: Describe a time you developed or revised an acquisition policy to implement a FAR change or an OMB initiative.
How would you brief senior leadership on competing procurement options?
How do you stay current on FAR overhauls and government-wide acquisition initiatives?
Tell us about overseeing a procurement program with compliance problems.
watch_outs: Daniel likely does not meet the 4-year contracting or GS-13-equivalent specialized experience requirement, and the posting enforces it strictly.
The posting requires a degree with 24 business-related credit hours, verified by transcripts.
The job is in DC with only partial telework, so expect a commute from Manassas (VRE is an option).
